clue.text: Distant relative extremely touched

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its very first and very last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of relative
touched in the sense of emotionally affected

explanation.surface: A far-flung cousin turns out to be very emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distant relative' reads as one phrase, as in a cousin twice removed, but only the first word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something removed from a place is far away from it, so the adjective is a synonym for remote or aloof.

clue.text: Perfect beer on the counter in Crown & Sceptre?

indicators.note: counter suggests running contrary, so the letters read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: A1 means perfect, with the 1 read as I
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A perfect pint is served across the bar at the Crown & Sceptre pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown & Sceptre reads as a pub name, fitting the beer and bar counter; really it gives examples of royal emblems.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the emblems of royalty, such as the crown and sceptre, hence the question mark for examples.

clue.text: After discharging wind, dairy cow's cry is starting to get angry

indicators.note: discharging means letting out, so those letters are released from the word

blocks.note: the sound a cow makes
taken as written
air is wind

explanation.surface: A flatulent cow in the dairy is getting cross.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed dairy goes after the cow's cry, as 'After' at the front tells you.
explanation.definitionFit: Moody describes someone sullen or bad-tempered, a close match for angry.

clue.text: Crime-fighter's leaving it in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means in a mess, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crime-fighter walks away from a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante is a private person who takes it on themselves to punish crime without legal authority.

clue.text: Some Guardian Angels hunting female

indicators.note: Some means only part of the words that follow is wanted

blocks.note: inside the two words

explanation.surface: Some members of the Guardian Angels street patrol are out hunting a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana was the Roman goddess of the hunt, a female huntress.

clue.text: Roast meat with unlimited macaroni, for example

indicators.note: unlimited means without its limits, so the word's two end letters are cut away

blocks.note: lamb is a kind of meat
macaroni is an example of pasta, which loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A Sunday roast of meat served with a heap of macaroni.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roast' looks like cooking, but it is the verb meaning to criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to mock or criticise them severely, which is what lambasting means.

clue.text: Court official's note on sentence

blocks.note: drop someone a line means send a note
to judge someone is to pass sentence

explanation.surface: A law court clerk writes a note on a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal surface hides a tennis court; in a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A line judge is the tennis official who calls whether the ball has landed in or out.

clue.text: Represents wealth

blocks.note: first meaning: stands for, signifies
second meaning: money and resources

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a phrase about being a symbol of riches; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb form signifies or stands for, while the noun denotes financial resources or income.

clue.text: Every year returning docile accommodating Conservative candidate

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the abbreviation is read in the other direction
accommodating means giving room to, so one word houses the other

blocks.note: per annum, abbreviated p.a.
pliant means compliant or docile
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Each year a meek Tory candidate comes back to stand again.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicant for a post is a candidate for it.

clue.text: Difficult to carry on this evening

indicators.note: to carry means to hold, so one word bears the other inside it

blocks.note: a tight spot is a difficult one
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is hard to keep going this evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry on' reads as one phrase meaning continue; here carry is the container and on is the letters held.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is the present or coming evening, an adverb meaning on this evening.

clue.text: Ringo Starr occasionally playing on good material

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of the drummer's surname is kept
playing suggests the letters are performing loosely, free to fall into a new order

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
taken as written
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: The Beatles' drummer drumming away on something good.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'X on Y' puts X after Y, so the jumbled letters follow G.
explanation.definitionFit: Grosgrain is a heavy ribbed silk or rayon fabric, often used for ribbons, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Poplar, East London — finally pursuing 18's killer?

indicators.note: finally picks out the final letter of the word just before it
something pursuing comes behind, so these letters are placed after the next piece

blocks.note: Cleopatra, the answer at 18, died from the bite of an asp
E is the compass abbreviation
the last letter of London

explanation.surface: Poplar in east London is chasing a killer, like a crime story.
explanation.walkthrough: Poplar is a district of East London, which is why 'East London' reads as an address; here Poplar is the tree and the place words are just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a species of poplar tree, known for leaves that tremble in the slightest breeze.

clue.text: Reliable, possibly stainless steel cycles

indicators.note: cycles means the word goes round, its leading letters moving to the back in turn

blocks.note: stainless steel is an example of an alloy, hence possibly

explanation.surface: Stainless steel bicycles are dependable machines.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the first two letters of the metal mixture to the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal friend is faithful and can be depended upon, so the word is a synonym for reliable.

clue.text: Settling a puppy recently arrived to replace Oscar

indicators.note: to replace means one item is taken out and another set in its place

blocks.note: taken as written
a puppy is a young dog
just in means recently arrived
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A household settling down a new puppy that has just come home.
explanation.walkthrough: The O of the young dog is swapped out for the phrase meaning recently arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusting is the process of becoming accustomed to new circumstances, which is what settling in involves.

clue.text: Tragedy of American theatre yet to work with Aaron Copland

indicators.note: to work means set to operate on, so the following letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
the National Theatre is abbreviated NT
taken as written
the American composer's name taken as written

explanation.surface: An American theatre company yet to stage a tragedy with music by Copland.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play about the Roman general and the Egyptian queen is one of his great tragedies.

clue.text: Queen Anne tiles must go outside large shed and hide plants

indicators.note: shed means cast off, so that letter is dropped from the word
must go suggests the letters move about and are rearranged
outside means the rearranged letters are placed around the monarch

blocks.note: R, for Regina, is the Latin for queen
taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Queen Anne style tiles must be removed from a big shed before planting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Anne' reads as the architectural style but splits into two pieces; 'shed' is a verb, not a garden building, and 'hide plants' means works where hides are processed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanneries are factories, or plants, where animal hides are turned into leather.

clue.text: Catch tie dancing around close to Ginger Rogers maybe

indicators.note: dancing around means moving every which way, so the letters swirl into a new order
close to means the end of the following word, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of Ginger

explanation.surface: Ginger Rogers catches her partner's tie while dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ginger Rogers is Fred Astaire's dancing partner, but the clue splits her name: Ginger gives a letter and Rogers is Richard Rogers, designer of the Lloyd's building and the Millennium Dome.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Rogers was a leading British architect, so the answer is his profession, signalled by maybe.

clue.text: Praise lieutenant after chopper comes back

indicators.note: comes back means the word travels backwards, read from right to left
after places the officer's abbreviation behind the other piece

blocks.note: an axe is a tool for chopping
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: An officer is praised after a helicopter returns safely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' suggests a helicopter, but here it is the tool for chopping wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to praise them highly or raise them up in honour.

clue.text: Former partner's preoccupied dear

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
pensive means lost in thought

explanation.surface: An ex-partner is lost in thought about a beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like a term of endearment, but it means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of high-priced is a synonym for expensive.

clue.text: Rod's handling old boat

indicators.note: has handling means holding in the hands, so one word grips the other inside it

blocks.note: a cane is a rod or stick
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A man called Rod is steering an ancient vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name; it is the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow boat paddled by hand.

clue.text: Some of Galloway's issues with party initially being overwhelmed by smears

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used
being overwhelmed by means swamped and engulfed, so these letters are put inside the next word

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
the first letter of party
smears as in coats of paint or grease

explanation.surface: A politician named Galloway's party problems are smeared in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: Smears gives COATS, which wraps around the abbreviation for with and the party's first letter. Galloway is not the politician but a Scottish breed of cattle, and their issues are what they drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowpats are what cattle such as the Galloway breed leave behind, so they are literally some of its issues, or output.

clue.text: See 13
Boss supporting utter idiot

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means sitting underneath, so this piece goes below the other

blocks.note: to air a view is to utter it
the head is the boss

explanation.surface: A manager is backing a complete fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective, as in utter idiot, but it is the verb meaning to say.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is a slang term for a stupid, empty-headed person.

clue.text: Unemployed nursing student follows women's sport

indicators.note: nursing means cradling, so one word holds the other within it
follows puts these letters after the abbreviation that comes first

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for women
resting is the actor's euphemism for being out of work
L for learner, a student

explanation.surface: A jobless nurse takes up a women's sport.
explanation.walkthrough: An out-of-work actor is said to be resting.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrestling is a combat sport in which two people grapple to throw or pin each other.

clue.text: Handle championship

blocks.note: first meaning: a name, as in someone's handle
second meaning: a sporting crown, as in a world heavyweight belt

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to cope with a competition; both words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a name or form of address, and a sporting championship won is also called this.

clue.text: Revolting illness not unknown when eating last of Jamie Oliver's food

indicators.note: not means without, so the following letter is dropped
revolting means turning over, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the lurgy is British slang for an unspecified illness
y is an algebraic unknown
the final letter of Jamie

explanation.surface: A disgusting bug caught from eating the TV chef Jamie Oliver's cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: Jamie Oliver is a celebrity chef, but the name splits: Jamie gives a letter and Oliver is Oliver Twist, who asked for more of this.
explanation.definitionFit: In Oliver Twist the workhouse boys are fed thin porridge, and Oliver famously asks for more of it.

clue.text: All-time low as papers printed covers about …

indicators.note: covers means wraps over, so one word is put around the other
about means turned round, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a newspaper ran a story when it printed it
identity papers are ID

explanation.surface: Newspapers hit a record low over what they printed.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into 25 across, but each is a separate clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, literally the point of the sky directly below an observer.

clue.text: Shot a serious film

blocks.note: a dram is a small shot of spirits
taken as written

explanation.surface: A director shot a serious movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like filming; it is a measure of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a film or play of serious rather than comic character.

clue.text: … famous gangster first

first written as 1st, with the figure read as the letter I

explanation.definitionFit: A-list celebrities are the most famous and sought-after, so the term serves as an adjective for well known.

clue.text: Explain journalist hosting launch is oddly worried

indicators.note: oddly means in odd positions, so the first, third, fifth and seventh letters are kept
hosting means having a guest inside, so the journalist's letters surround the others

blocks.note: an ed is an editor, crosswords' usual journalist
the odd-placed letters of the two words
worried as in ate away at, gnawed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' means fretted, but also gnawed, as something eating at you.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to make something clear, which is to explain it.

clue.text: Dodgy cult's inspiring marketing feature

a unique selling point, abbreviated USP, is a marketing term

explanation.definitionFit: Something suspect is of doubtful honesty or reliability, which is what dodgy means informally.

clue.text: A welder moved downwind

blocks.note: taken as written
